aliases: Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos

intervals.label: observatory officially inaugurated
intervals.locator: IAC history page, section on the 1980s
intervals.note: The date is the official inauguration, not a first-observation date; no source read dates the first observation. The same page dates the agreement that internationalised the observatory earlier: "Thus on May 26th 1979 Spain signed, with Denmark, Sweden, and the United Kingdom, in Santa Cruz de La Palma the “Agreement and Protocol of Cooperation in Astrophysics” by which the Teide Observatory (Tenerife) and the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory (La Palma) were internationalised".
intervals.quote: In 1985 the Official Inauguration of the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias and the Teide and Roque de los Muchachos Observatories took place

intervals.label: hosts gamma-ray telescopes
intervals.note: Start is MAGIC-I's October 2003 operational start. HEGRA (experiment:hegra, a separate record) took data at the site from 1987 to 2002, and the observatory's own start is the 1985 inauguration in the first interval.
intervals.quote: started operations in its final configuration in October 2003

name: Roque de los Muchachos Observatory
notes: This facility is shared: experiment:ctao and experiment:magic both list it in their facility roles.

The observatory's start is the 1985 official inauguration (IAC history page), earlier than HEGRA (1987) and MAGIC (2003); the second interval records when MAGIC-I began gamma-ray work here, not the observatory's founding. Status 'active' reflects that the hosted experiments are operating (checked 2026-09-17).

operator.note: CTAO's own page names La Palma, Spain as one of its two array sites without naming a local operator; the Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias is the well-known operator of the wider Roque de los Muchachos Observatory, but that specific operator statement was not seen in any source consulted (checked 2026-09-17).
operator.quote: La Palma, Spain, and Paranal, Chile
operator.value: Instituto de Astrofísica de Canarias (host observatory); CTAO-North hosted here per CTAO's own site listing

summary.plain: A mountaintop observatory on the Spanish Canary Island of La Palma that hosts several gamma-ray telescopes, including MAGIC and the northern half of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory.
summary.technical: Astronomical observatory on the island of La Palma, Canary Islands, Spain, hosting the MAGIC telescopes and CTAO-North (the northern array of the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory).
